items.title: WHO guideline for non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults in primary and community care settings
items.citation: World Health Organization. WHO guideline for non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults in primary and community care settings. Geneva: WHO; 2023. ISBN 978-92-4-008178-9.
items.population: Adults, including older adults, with chronic primary low back pain in primary or community care.
items.intervention: Structured exercise therapy or programmes, among other non-surgical interventions considered by the guideline.
items.result: The guideline states that structured exercise therapy or a programme may be offered as part of care.
items.recommendation: Conditional recommendation in favour of use; low certainty evidence.
items.editorialDecision: No single modality, frequency, intensity, session duration or progression rule is presented here as a universal prescription. Individual assessment and contextual tailoring remain necessary.
items.limitations: Applies to chronic primary low back pain in adults. It does not establish applicability to acute pain, secondary causes, red flags, or an individual patient without assessment.
items.reviewStatus: bibliographic facts checked; professional clinical review pending

items.title: Effectiveness of progressive tendon-loading exercise therapy in patients with patellar tendinopathy: a randomised clinical trial
items.authors: Breda SJ, Oei EHG, Zwerver J, et al.
items.citation: Breda SJ, Oei EHG, Zwerver J, et al. Effectiveness of progressive tendon-loading exercise therapy in patients with patellar tendinopathy: a randomised clinical trial. Br J Sports Med. 2021;55(9):501-509.
items.population: 76 athletes aged 18-35 years with clinically diagnosed and ultrasound-confirmed patellar tendinopathy; mostly chronic symptoms; 38 per group.
items.intervention: Progressive tendon-loading exercise (PTLE) compared with eccentric exercise therapy (EET), over 24 weeks. The PTLE protocol included consecutive isometric, isotonic, energy-storage and sport-specific stages, progressed according to individual pain response.
items.result: At 24 weeks, adjusted between-group difference in VISA-P was 9 points in favour of PTLE (95% CI 1 to 16; p=0.023). Return to sport, satisfaction and adherence did not differ significantly between groups.
items.certainty: Single randomized trial; no GRADE certainty rating assigned in this app.
items.editorialDecision: The trial protocol is shown as a study finding, not as an individual treatment recommendation or universal dose.
items.limitations: Participants were athletic adults 18-35 with imaging-confirmed diagnosis; most had chronic symptoms and prior treatment. Only one participant was in the early-symptom stratum. Results may not generalize to children, older adults, non-athletes, other diagnoses or all care settings.
items.reviewStatus: bibliographic facts checked; professional clinical review pending

additionalSources.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management. NICE guideline NG59. Updated 2026.
additionalSources.population: People aged 16 and over with low back pain and sciatica.
additionalSources.intervention: Assessment and management guidance, including referral pathways for suspected cauda equina syndrome and other serious causes.
additionalSources.result: The guideline includes an interactive cauda equina pathway and emphasizes assessment of serious causes before routine management.
additionalSources.certainty: Guideline; no GRADE certainty claim copied into this app.
additionalSources.limitations: A red-flag list cannot exclude serious disease by itself. Clinical assessment and local urgent-care pathways apply.
additionalSources.reviewStatus: bibliographic facts checked; professional clinical review pending

additionalSources.citation: Corvos-Hidalgo CA, Bizzozero-Peroni B, Fernandez-Gimenez S, Pintos-Toledo E. Concordancia entre ecuaciones de predicción y el método de 1RM en cuatro ejercicios de entrenamiento resistido. Educación Física y Ciencia. 2022;24(2):e222.
additionalSources.population: 30 young adults experienced in resistance exercise.
additionalSources.intervention: Comparison of Brzycki, Epley and other prediction equations with measured 1RM in squat, bench press, deadlift and military press; sets included 1-7 repetitions.
additionalSources.result: Agreement varied by equation and exercise; the study supports treating estimates as exercise-specific rather than interchangeable.
additionalSources.certainty: Validation study; no GRADE rating assigned.
additionalSources.limitations: Small sample of experienced young adults and four lifts. The app accepts no more than seven repetitions to stay within this study's tested range; results may not generalize to other people or exercises. Output is not an observed maximum or clinical prescription.
additionalSources.reviewStatus: bibliographic facts checked; professional clinical review pending

additionalSources.citation: Zourdos MC, Goldsmith JA, Helms ER, et al. Proximity to failure and total repetitions performed in a set influences accuracy of intraset repetitions in reserve-based rating of perceived exertion. J Strength Cond Res. 2021;35(Suppl 1):S158-S165.
additionalSources.population: 25 trained men; mean age 25.3 years; squat set at 70% of 1RM to failure.
additionalSources.intervention: Participants predicted repetitions in reserve at specified points during one set, then continued to failure.
additionalSources.result: Prediction error was larger farther from failure and during longer sets in the observed protocol.
additionalSources.certainty: Single laboratory study; no GRADE rating assigned.
additionalSources.limitations: Small all-male trained sample and a single squat protocol; it does not establish accuracy for every person, exercise, or clinical population.
additionalSources.reviewStatus: bibliographic facts checked; professional clinical review pending

additionalSources.citation: Franklin BA, Eijsvogels TMH, Pandey A, Quindry J, Toth PP. Physical activity, cardiorespiratory fitness, and cardiovascular health: a clinical practice statement of the American Society for Preventive Cardiology Part II: physical activity, cardiorespiratory fitness, minimum and goal intensities for exercise training, prescriptive methods, and special patient populations. Am J Prev Cardiol. 2022;12:100425.
additionalSources.population: Clinical practice statement spanning healthy adults and special patient populations.
additionalSources.intervention: Evidence review of methods for determining exercise intensity, including target heart rate derived from heart-rate reserve.
additionalSources.result: The heart-rate-reserve method calculates a mathematical target from maximal and resting heart rates plus a chosen intensity fraction.
additionalSources.certainty: Clinical practice statement; no GRADE rating copied into this app.
additionalSources.limitations: Age-predicted maximums may misestimate values in some groups; medication and cardiovascular conditions can limit heart-rate interpretation. The calculator requires measured inputs and does not select intensity.
additionalSources.reviewStatus: bibliographic facts checked; professional clinical review pending
